item.title: Coal gasification scheme attracts just two bids in its third round
item.description: Limited participation in the third round highlights financing and technology challenges, with industry calling for credit guarantees and greater lender confidence to attract investment ...
item.dc:creator: Saket Kumar
item.content:encoded: With just two bids received in its third round, the Centre’s ₹37,500-crore coal gasification incentive scheme has continued to see limited industry participation, highlighting the challenges of attracting investment into a capital-intensive industry despite substantial government support. According to a notice issued by the Ministry of Coal, one bid each was received under Category 2, meant for private-sector companies and government public sector undertakings (PSUs), and Category 3, which covers demonstration projects using indigenous technology and/or small-scale product-based plants. Talcher Chemicals Private Limited, the sole bidder under Category 2, and Carbon Chemical Private Limited, the sole bidder under Category 3, have been declared technically qualified and made eligible to open their financial bids. The response follows seven applications in the first round and two in the second, both submitted by state-run NTPC. The limited participation across three rounds raises questions about what it will take to attract a wider pool of investors to India’s coal gasification sector. Coal gasification converts coal into synthesis gas, or syngas, which can be used to manufacture products such as methanol, ammonia, synthetic natural gas, hydrogen, fertilisers, and other chemicals. The scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet in May 2026, has an outlay of ₹37,500 crore and aims to support projects that gasify around 75 million tonnes of coal and lignite. It is intended to contribute towards India’s target of achieving 100 million tonnes of coal gasification capacity by 2030. The government expects the initiative to attract investments of ₹2.5-3 trillion and reduce dependence on high-value imported industrial feedstock. Atanu Mukherjee, chief executive officer of Dastur Energy, said the limited response should not necessarily be interpreted as a lack of industry interest, but rather as a reflection of the challenges in translating interest into commercially viable and financeable projects. Dastur Energy provides coal gasification consultancy to companies. “Viability Gap Funding (VGF) is an excellent mechanism for improving project economics and incentivising capital investment. However, improving project economics and making a project bankable are two different things,” Mukherjee said. Financial institutions remain cautious about lending to capital-intensive projects of this nature, particularly where domestic commercial operating precedents are limited, and technology and implementation risks are perceived to be high, Mukherjee said. Equity investors seek greater visibility on the availability and cost of debt, while lenders require certainty around technology performance, project execution and long-term commercial viability, he added. He said the government could complement the existing incentive framework with a partial credit guarantee mechanism to reduce lenders’ risks and encourage greater participation from financial institutions. Technology suited to India’s high-ash coal and the availability of assured buyers for the products are other important considerations for prospective investors, he said. Mukherjee suggested that India facilitate the licensing of proven international technologies, including suitable Chinese technologies, through domestic technology companies to build engineering, equipment manufacturing and execution capabilities. He also called for the development of standardised modular gasification systems processing around 500-1,500 tonnes of coal per day, depending on feedstock and industrial application. Such projects could widen participation beyond a handful of large industrial groups, while generating operating experience and improving confidence among lenders, he said. Long-term offtake arrangements with fertiliser, chemical, steel and energy companies could improve revenue visibility for projects. However, assured buyers alone would not ensure commercial viability, Mukherjee said, adding that coal-derived products would need to remain competitive with imported alternatives.

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / OPEC+ may roll over current oil output targets at its Sunday meeting

OPEC+ may roll over current oil output targets at its Sunday meeting OPEC+ is expected to maintain current oil output targets at Sunday's meeting as the Iran war disrupts Middle East exports, though sources said no decision has been reached.

OPEC+ may keep its current oil output targets unchanged at Sunday's meeting as the Iran war disrupts exports from member countries in the Middle East, according to sources. | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 1 min read Last Updated : Nov 26 2026 | 5:32 PM IST

Listen to This Article

OPEC+ may roll over its current oil output targets at a meeting on Sunday, two people with knowledge of the matter said, as the Iran war continues to disrupt exports from the group's members in the Middle East.   No decision has been reached, they said, and talks continue ahead of Sunday's meeting.   Oil analyst firm Rapidan also expects no changes in OPEC+ targets on Sunday.   "Given infrastructure damage and uncertainty over the conflict's duration and lasting impact on production and exports, we expect ministers to maintain existing targets and postpone major quota decisions until next year, 2027," Rapidan said in a report.   More From This Section

item.description: The charitable entities controlling the Tata Group are set to challenge N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons chairman ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / Tata Trusts to challenge Chandrasekaran's reappointment in Bombay HC

Tata Trusts to challenge Chandrasekaran's reappointment in Bombay HC The charitable entities controlling the Tata Group are set to challenge N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons chairman

The dispute follows N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons executive chairman for another five years at the September 17 board meeting

Press Trust of India Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 26 2026 | 10:40 AM IST

Listen to This Article

The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the R.D. Tata Trust (RDTT) will file suits in the Bombay High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a second five-year term. The SDTT will seek ₹50 crore and RDTT will seek ₹15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest. As per the suits, the September 17 decision to reappoint Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association. The dispute follows N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons executive chairman for another five years at the September 17 board meeting.

The two trusts voted on Wednesday night to pass the resolutions to move HC as there was a lack of any satisfactory replies to the communications sent by them since September 17. Also Read

Now, Noel wants revision of Tata Sons board agenda, pushes restructuring

RBI has already answered its own listing question in case of Tata Sons premium

Tata Sons defers board meeting to Nov 30 as Noel asks for 7-day notice

Tata Sons board meet postponed to Nov 30 after Noel raises concerns

RBI Act may show the way on Tata Sons listing amid regulatory uncertainty premium

The immediate relief being sought is to ensure that the chairman during the November 30 meeting is prevented from exercising his casting vote in the event of a split in opinion among nominee directors. Tata Trusts, chaired by Noel Tata, holds around 66 per cent of Tata Sons and has challenged the board resolution passed on September 17. In its September 20 statement, the Trusts said the resolution was not validly passed and had "no legal effect".

At the centre of the dispute are Tata Sons' Articles of Association (AoA) and special rights given to Trusts-nominated directors. It has two nominee directors on its board -- Noel Tata and Venu Srinivasan. On September 17, Noel Tata voted against Chandrasekaran's reappointment, while Venu Srinivasan supported it. As per Trusts, both nominated directors were required to support the decision. In its statement issued in September, the Trusts said the AoA of Tata Sons provide that no decision can be taken unless it has the affirmative support of at least a majority of the Directors nominated by the Tata Trusts. "This is a separate condition under the AoA," it said, pointing out that the AoA does not leave any decision of the board to a mere head count of directors.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: New US tariff may give India edge over Asian peers if trade deal done: GTRI
item.description: GTRI said a proposed 17% US tariff under a trade pact would give India a slight edge over Asian competitors, while the rate could rise to 25% without an agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / New US tariff may give India edge over Asian peers if trade deal done: GTRI

New US tariff may give India edge over Asian peers if trade deal done: GTRI GTRI said a proposed 17% US tariff under a trade pact would give India a slight edge over Asian competitors, while the rate could rise to 25% without an agreement.

India's proposed tariff rate under a potential US trade pact could be lower than those faced by several Asian competitors, giving Indian exporters a slight advantage, according to GTRI. | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 26 2026 | 12:11 AM IST

Listen to This Article

India could face a 17 per cent US tariff if a bilateral trade agreement is finalised, giving it a slight edge over several Asian competitors, but the rate could rise to 25 per cent without a pact, think tank GTRI said on Wednesday, warning of possible additional duties or import quotas.   India must reject the trade deal and instead answer allegations sector by sector, it said.   The answers should clearly show that India's investment serves domestic buyers, overseas customers, and future demand, the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) said.   "Under the proposed USTR tariffs, Indian imports face a 17 per cent tariff if a trade pact is finalised, offering a calculated 1 per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate), while rising up to 25 per cent without a deal, alongside the risk that an adverse USTR ruling could bring further duties or import quotas," GTRI Founder Ajay Srivastava said.

These new tariffs proposed on November 25 by the US Trade Representative (USTR) were under Section 301 excess-capacity investigations. Also Read

Section 301 probe: India rejects US claim of structural excess capacity

US proposes up to 25% tariff on India, offers 17% upon trade deal

Trump rebuilds global tariff wall, India faces proposed duties of up to 25%

US proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including India and China

Asian stocks tumble as AI rebound stumbles, US tariff threats loom

Initiated by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) on March 11, 2026, against 16 economies, the proposed duties target 14 trading partners while excluding Mexico and Norway for now.   "By deploying a dual-rate structure, threatening steep baseline tariffs against countries that refuse a pact while offering lower rates to those that sign, Washington reclaims the bargaining power to impose duties at will and extract unilateral concessions, allowing a government to secure tariff relief even if the industrial capacity that prompted the investigation remains unchanged," he said.

For India, the Section 301 investigation flags potential excess capacity or export surpluses across seven sectors: solar modules (where capacity is nearly triple domestic demand), petrochemicals, steel, textiles, health-related goods, construction materials, and automotive products.   More From This Section
